title: Owned HTTPS to WebSocket upgrade handoff
summary: Rasen Falcon/Wire wss traffic should upgrade inside the owned ooRexx HTTPS server without exposing its TCP/TLS internals. HTTPS owns admission, TLS and HTTP parsing; WebSocket receives a parsed Upgrade request, plaintext duplex wrapper, peer/address projection and any post-header bytes.
invariants: The HTTPS server remains sole owner of accepted TCP sockets, TLS/OpenSSL state, certificates, bounded worker admission and TLS generation lifetime.
The ordinary HTTPS route/interceptor boundary must not be widened to expose raw Socket/BIO/SSL objects.
A dedicated upgrade adapter may construct WebSocketUpgradeRequest from the already parsed HTTP head.
The plaintext duplex wrapper continues reads/writes through the established HTTPS TLS session; it is not a native socket.
Any bytes already read after the HTTP header terminator must be passed as initialReceiveBuffer so the first WebSocket frame is not lost.
A successful 101 switches that connection into upgraded mode; ordinary HTTP body/routing/pipelining must not resume.
The HTTPS worker/admission/TLS generation lease remains alive until the upgraded wrapper closes.
Rejected upgrades stay in normal HTTPS response handling.
This seam directly supports Rasen Falcon/Wire browser duplex traffic over the project's own HTTPS/TLS platform code.

provenance.claim: Contract fixture for parsed HTTPS handoff and already-read first frame.
Stable HTTPS API documents transport hiding and bounded admission; exact counterpart revision must be reconciled by its owner before live qualification.
